slides: Your muscles don’t remember the weight, they remember the pattern.
Every rep writes a neural map that tells your body how to recruit fibers.
If the map repeats unchanged, the brain sees no need to upgrade.
Add a micro‑increase—2‑5%—or a new angle every 2 weeks and the map rewrites.
Small, regular variations outpace occasional massive lifts.
Decision fatigue is the silent thief of ambition.
Each choice burns a finite reserve of willpower.
When the reserve runs low, you default to the path of least resistance.
Batch routine decisions—clothes, meals, routes—into a single planning block.
Conserve will for the choices that truly matter.
Your body’s best workout happens under the sheets.
During deep sleep, growth hormone spikes and glycogen stores refill.
Without that window, muscles stay in catabolic mode.
Aim for 90 minutes of uninterrupted REM cycles, not just 7 hours on the clock.
Prioritize sleep blocks as rigorously as you schedule lifts.
Alignment isn’t a buzzword; it’s a friction test.
When your actions match your core values, internal resistance drops.
Low friction means less mental energy spent on justification.
Audit one habit today: ask if it serves your ‘why’ or just your habit.
Keep only actions that reduce internal drag; discard the rest.
